# BOOK 1: "Footprints" (Kay Cleaver Strahan, 1929) — Notes

**Setting/Frame:** Portland, Oregon hotel (the Trensonian), 1928. Judith Quilter Whitefield (widow, ~50s) visits her brother Neal Quilter (46) at hotel. Judith's grandfather's locket: "Judith Quilter. Achieve tranquillity." Judith's husband Gregory Whitefield died (Colorado). Judith's car driver George; her sister-in-law... Ursula (Neal's love, widow, Italian-born, "Q 2" ranch). Chris (Christopher Quilter, Judith's cousin, married to Irene, a chatterbox). Lucy Quilter Cerini (sister, writer; husband Cerini; "babies"). Dr. Joe Elm (white-haired, fat, ~70s, old family doctor, "Bless my soul to glory", "send you a bill"). Dr. Koreth (Vienna psychiatrist visited Q 2).

**Neal's confession (Ch. I):** Says he killed Father (Richard "Dick" Quilter, shot 8 Oct 1900 at Q 2 Ranch, Quilter County, eastern Oregon; locked in rooms; snow fell; no footprints; rope from attic out window; bed moved). Neal was 18 then. Aunt Gracia Quilter (mystic, Siloamite). Olympe (Phineas's wife; actress; red mask/satin from her gown; ".32 Colt's"). Grandfather Thaddeus Quilter (80 in 1900, Schiller translator). Uncle Phineas (67, gold-hunter, Dr. Joe's room in Portland). Irene (Chris's second wife, ex-husband Archie Biggil). Dong Lee (Chinese house boy). Judith (Judy) at Colorado with husband Greg. Judith received letters.

**Ch. II:** Lynn MacDonald, San Francisco crime analyst (red hair, gray eyes). Dr. Elm hires her; she reads letters. Dr. Elm's history: Quilter family pattern from 1624 Sir Christopher Quilter in Virginia; 1848 Christopher & Thaddeus moved to Oregon; Phineas (b. 1833), Olympe (married Phineas after war), Dick (married young; wife died), Gracia (lost love Enos Karabass; Dick killed Enos ~1883), Christopher (Chris, son of elder Christopher), Irene, Neal, Lucy (12 in 1900). Missionaries Mr. Cordinger & Mr. Withmore; Dong Lee at dentist. Dr. Elm cash: $1,004.20 debt joke. Dick's insurance policy ($10,000 accidental death) paid by Dr. Elm for $40 premium.

**Letters (Ch. III–XIX):** Lucy's letters (Mar–Sep 1900): Irene arrived March 9 with Chris; Grandfather's rule "Achieve tranquillity"-type rules; Uncle Phineas "Be wise. Use Wisdom's Robertine". Q 2 mortgaged; Chris wanted to sell ranch; Irene's "Booful"; Irene's first husband Archie Biggil (importer, Brazil). Chris's play "Gold". Phineas to Nome. Chris moved into cupola room; Irene and Chris exchanged rooms with Dick. Dick baptized Siloamite 1900 (at Quilter River, with missionaries) — Dick had cancer (per later confession), Olympe's gun. Olympe's "God help the Quilter wives" speech. Neal's sonnets joke; Chris "Booful". Dick's wagon tongue accident over Quilter Mountain (Indian Charles 3 O X). Sale offer by land company; $9,000 leftover.

**Neal's letters (Oct 10–Nov 12 1900):** Neal's account of the night: Monday 8 Oct; Irene downstairs; Irene's keys; rope; snow; 11:50 shot; Lucy in Neal's room; Chris's clock 11:45; Olympe found fainted with gun. Grandfather: "He has escaped some other way". Aunt Gracia's accusations, Irene's story ("Red mask", "Got away", "Bring Father. I must tell him."). Inquest at Quilterville Friday 12 Oct; coroner Hank Buckerman; prosecutor Benjamin Thopson; defense Bruno Ward. Insurance $10,000; Dr. Elm's birth call (Mrs. H. F. Ferndell). Aunt Gracia's testimony: rope, lamp, "trap me". Funeral Sat 13 Oct, Siloamite rites. Olympe's Chapter XVIII false-confession theory; Lucy claims Olympe shot Dick by accident. Uncle Phineas's $45,000 mine deposit (Malheur County). Grandfather died night of 30 Oct? (Neal: "night before he died" — Grandfather died ~31 Oct). Lucy sent to Judith (leaves Thursday 25 Oct). Neal to Oregon Agricultural College Feb.

**Ch. XX–XXI:** Lynn MacDonald finishes letters; Miss Kingsbury secretary. Second meeting with Dr. Elm: Richard had adeno carcinoma of liver; Richard took no opiate; Dr. Elm confesses he killed Dick (Ch. XXI, at Q 2 by Dr. Elm's account; Dick planned insurance death, Dick and Elm together; Dick's plan; Dick used "red mask" for Dr. Elm?). Judith hears Dr. Joe; Neal's "boil" analysis; Dr. Elm tells Neal "I killed Dick." Neal then realizes Grandfather was the one who helped Dick ("He wasn't afraid to tell me. I mean, Dr. Joe—Grandfather.").

Final scene: the "I killed Dick" confession by Dr. Joe, Neal's rejection, and Neal concludes that Grandfather (Thaddeus) was the one who planned/participated. Children playing (Baby Thad, Delidah, Chris's sons). Schumann's Abendlied; Ursula plays.

**Note:** Some details ambiguous in source; Grandfather's rule "Be generous rather than just"; Lucy's letters signed "Lucy"; Neal's letters "Your loving brother, Neal."

# BOOK 2: "The Cruise of the Gyro-Car" (Herbert Strang, 1911)

**Characters:** George Buckland (18, Winchester/Cambridge-bound, inventor of gyro-car; monoplane/mono-rail adaptation of Louis Brennan's car, four tandem wheels, two gyroscopes), Maurice Buckland (elder brother, secretary at British agency, Sofia; formal speech; "old boy"), Sheila Buckland (sister), Mrs. Courtenay-Greene (Hon., aunt, dowager, pince-nez, The Acacias, Chertsey Road, Shepperton). Count Slavianski (= Max Mumm, spy, German; yellow racing car; "General Count"), Major Rostopchin (secretary; real name Ernst Böhmer, ex-sergeant), Hang? no — Austrian spies.

**Plot:**
- Early June/July; Maurice home on leave from Sofia; Shepperton; George's car crashes into wall near Anchor Hotel; repaired; gyroscopes.
- Count Slavianski's party stalk Maurice; Foreign Office (Secretary of state) gives despatch for Sofia re Balkan crisis (Austria vs Montenegro, Serbia; Bulgaria's attitude). Maurice takes route via Brindisi.
- Bags switched at Sunbury (Maurice's bag empty; Count's secretary took it). Maurice's black official bag. Despatch concealed in gyro-car engine (George hides it in mechanism).
- Chase: Waterloo, Grand Hotel, Herne Hill, Dover (Admiralty launch; Lieutenant), Calais (Gare Maritime; Custom House). Paris (Hotel St. James, Rue Royale); Champ Elysées; Melun (plank across excavation; Count's men trap; gyro-car runs plank). Montereau, Sens, Dijon, Beaune, Romenay, Mantenay, St. Julien (geese), Montrevel, Bourg, Ambérieu, Aix-les-Bains, Chambéry (octroi), Modane (customs; "Austrians"), Turin (Hotel Europa), Alessandria, Genoa, Pisa, Leghorn, Volterra, Siena, Rome (British Stores), Naples, Eboli, Potenza, Ginosa, Taranto (Virgil), Brindisi (Count's motor; naval officer; torpedo-boat aground).
- Crossing Adriatic: skipper Antonio Fagazzi, smack *Margherita*, Villanuova; sail to Durazzo (Dyrrhachium). Chased by Austrian launch. Albanian interior: Tirana, Elbasan, Skumbi bridge.
- Giulika (old Albanian, kula, besa, Lek law), grandsons Marko, Doda, Dushmani; Giorgio (shot, blood-feud with Leka). Riddles (snail; candle; cow fell from cliff). Count holds Maurice; Maurice tricked by "Hey diddle diddle" cipher. Maurice tied; Giorgio cuts bonds; escape up gorge; Zutni's house; swamp crossed with planks; landslip; Black Drin rapids; Trebischte bridge; Giorgio's blood-foe Leka; Maurice wounded above right knee.
- Prizren; Turkish Pasha; race along plain (horse spooked by smoke); Morava; Sofia; despatch delivered (concealed in engine). Reward/King.
- Epilogue: Christmas with Giulika; feud settled with Maurice's money (~£25); Slavianski (lame) at Scutari, later in Vienna.

**Key phrases:** "Won by a neck!"; "Prevention is better than cure"; "Mieux vaut prévenir que guérir"; "Conspuez les Allemands!"; "Hey, diddle, diddle, Ze cat and ze fiddle"; "Tan giat tjeter" (Long life to you).

# BOOK 3: "The Young Naval Captain; or, The War of All Nations" (Ralph Bonehill, 1902)

**Setting:** 1936 war; US vs world (England, France, Germany, Russia, Japan, China...). President Jefferson McKinley Adams. Secretary of the Navy Short. Senator Forbish. Commodore David Pelham (father, dead). Commodore Garrison (Cuba). Admiral Fielding (Canada). Admiral Alvin Chester (Pacific).

**Characters:** Oscar Pelham (~20, inventor, captain; black hair, black eyes); Andy Greggs (18, first lieutenant, blue eyes, curly brown hair); George Dross (old engineer); Jim (sailor), Marney, Walton (ammunition man), Gilson; Martha Adams (President's daughter, brown eyes, kidnapped). Gabretti (Italian traitor who blew up Holland I). Lieutenant Raxtell (madman). Nathan Pargloss (embezzler, drowned). Hang Chang (Chinese captain). Captain Gresson (British, Corcoran). Captain Roquez (Spanish). Jean Fevre (French dude survivor).

**Events:**
- Holland I blown up by Gabretti; Oscar designs Holland XI (aluminum/steel, 115 ft; model tested Long Island Sound).
- Sandy Hook battle; Chicago sinks; German submarine sinks US cruisers.
- Secretary Short meeting; new Holland built in 30 days ($500,000).
- Tien-Tsin (Chinese armored cruiser) sunk off Baracoa, Cuba. Republique (French) sunk; Holland buried under wreck; shell fails.
- Japanese army (~1000) captures Oscar; rescued by Andy; dynamite bombs.
- Sargasso Sea escape; Lieutenant Raxtell's madness at Gulf of St. Lawrence; Terrible, Wilhelm II., Philippe sunk.
- Fraudulent message (kidnapped Martha Adams from White House, Washington); fake order near Cape Cod; copper netting mine; English despatch boat rammed.
- Casco Bay / Portland battle (Utah, Tennessee, Oregon, Brooklyn, New Jersey, Windsor, New York); Holland XI turns defeat to victory.
- Central American Canal: Pargloss plot, drowned.
- Honolulu: foreign fleet destroyed (Diamond Head); tidal wave strands Holland; Pekin, Tokio, Chinese ships sunk.
- Whale (Holland trap-door), Pacific storm; Cape Nome gold; Ivan II sunk; Hang Chang attacks Oscar.
- Spanish capture (Roquez, Gabretti) at Holland; recaptured; Santiago de Cuba.
- Underwater volcano/earthquake; French ship Bordeaux (Jean Fevre rescued); Green Dragon (Chinese) found; Martha Adams saved; Green Dragon torpedoed.
- War ends; Oscar becomes Rear Admiral Pelham; married Martha; Andy and George commodores.

# BOOK 4: "The House 'Round the Corner" (Gordon Holmes / Louis Tracy? — text titled by Gordon Holmes, 1919)

**Characters:** Robert Armathwaite (alias of Sir Robert Dalrymple, K.C.S.I., Indian Political; "Baluchi Bob"; 35-36; tall; sallow; former High Commissioner of Barapur). Walker & Son (house agents, Nuttonby, N. Riding Yorkshire): elder James Walker; younger James "Jim" Walker (sprightly, "nut", fond of Meg). Mrs. Jackson (cottage) and daughter Betty Jackson (apple-cheeked). Stephen Garth / Stephen Ogilvey (professor, philology/folklore, 54; "dad"). Marguérite "Meg" Garth/Ogilvey (22, brown hair, brown eyes; flaxen? no—brown hair). Mrs. Garth / Mrs. Ogilvey (Nanette, Lady Brand, Madeleine Nanette de Courtray). Percy Whittaker (Eurasian, sister Edith/Edie Suarez; weak, sprained ankle). Dr. Ferdinand "Uncle Ferdie" Scaife (Bellerby). Tom Bland (carrier), P.C. Leadbitter (Gordon Highlanders, Dargai), Begonia Smith (gardener), Miggles (postman), Sir Berkeley Hutton ("Mollie" Lady Hutton, "the Pup"), Mr. Dobb (solicitor, Holloway & Dobb), Mr. Banks (Nuttonby Gazette), Storr (chauffeur), Farmer Burt (Castle Farm), Morand (India Office), Mrs. Vansittart? (no, that is in Book 5).

**Plot:** Armathwaite rents Grange (house 'round the corner), Elmdale, eight miles from Nuttonby; ghost of Stephen Garth (hanged himself near grandfather clock in hall; Garth's body found 21 June, two years earlier). Stained glass Black Prince window casts ghostly shadow on June evenings. Armathwaite finds Meg hidden in loft (booby trap with Burmese gong). Meg in Percy's clothes (tweeds). Meg's story: father alive; mother and she went to Quimper/Cornwall (Warleggan). Armathwaite threatens Walker, kicks him out. Walker goes to Dobb; Banks; telegram from "Sigmatic" (India Office). Percy Whittaker sprains ankle falling down stairs (sees ghost). Percy forces Meg to marry him; Armathwaite smashes window glass (Black Prince's face). Mrs. Garth (Nanette, Lady Brand) arrives by car; Meg engaged to Armathwaite. Dalrymple's identity revealed (reinstated, Barapur). Stephen Garth's confession: brother James Ogilvey (embezzler, Birmingham bank) died in Grange of apoplexy; Garth hid it; wrote letter to coroner. Walker/Walker & Son "Black Prince" window replaced. Dalrymple marries Meg; they wed; honeymoon Paris/Continent. Last line: "Who'd ha' thought... Meg Garth to Sir Robert Dalrymple?" "Well, I didn't, for one!"

# BOOK 5: "The Pillar of Light" (Louis Tracy, 1904)

**Epigraph:** Matthew 7:25 ("the house... founded upon a rock").

**Setting:** Gulf Rock Light, Scilly Isles/Land's End, Cornwall; Penzance. Dedicated keeper Stephen Brand (50, ex-attaché Paris, baronet Sir Stephen Brand, 9th Bt of Lesser Hambledon, Northumberland; killed French fop in duel). Daughters: Constance Brand (19, brown hair, hazel eyes, adopted? no—natural daughter) and Enid Trevillion (19, flaxen hair, blue eyes; foundling; ~1 year old when found on 30 July 1885 (per text: "nineteen years on 22nd June"; found June 1885 ~ "Ten minutes"): named after Arthurian Enid by Brand; her linen marked "E. T."; gold brooch with emeralds forming four-leafed shamrock). Lieutenant John Percival "Jack" Stanhope, R.N. (son of Lady Margaret Stanhope; Tregarthen Lodge, Penzance; Enid's suitor). Ben Pollard (Cornish fisherman, boat *Daisy*). Jim Spence (lame ex-keeper, Marazion). Jones (ex-keeper, Pilchard and Seine inn). Bates (broke leg), Jackson (scalded). Mrs. Sheppard (nurse/housekeeper, Laburnum Cottage). Lady Margaret Stanhope. Cyrus J. Traill (Philadelphia millionaire, Enid's natural father; wife Etta/Edith? lost in *Esmeralda* 1885). Charles A. "Charlie" Pyne (nephew, Yale/Quaker, American). Mrs. Vansittart = Nanette (Madeleine Nanette de Courtray; Brand's first wife, Constance's mother; widow of Vansittart). Elsie and Mamie (children; Mrs. Taylor). Mr. Emmett (first officer, Chinook). Captain of Chinook (unnamed; ex-Princess Royal, renamed).

**Events:** Pyne rescues on Chinook (hurricane wreck, Jan); tanker. Shark fight: Brand kills shark, found baby (Enid) in 1885 in boat. Lighthouse 130 ft high; auriscope (Brand's invention). Constance & Enid arrive in *Daisy* with Ben & Jim; rocket signals; hurricane; Chinook strikes reef; 78 survivors. Brand sends oil on water to calm sea; Stanhope rescues via rope and boat; food shipments via tug. Mrs. Vansittart nearly reveals. Traill arrives; letter reveals Enid is his daughter. Hotel dinner; Brand meets Nanette; she faints. Brand explains marriage history. Nanette arrives at cottage; reconciliation; she and Brand remarry; Constance and Enid weddings (Stanhope; Pyne). Last line: "Sir Stephen... the lighthouse ... winking portentously."

---

End of notes.
